subject: Chainmap & Custody Ledger Request — KMS and Subprocessor Catalog
messages:
From: Ava Solano <ava.solano@novamed.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novamed.com
Date: Mon, 28 Apr 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Request: chainmap / custody ledger for SOC2 audit

Hi Karthik,

We're starting our SOC 2 evidence collection and the auditor wants a compact 'chainmap' that ties Redwood's inference runtime to all third-party dependencies that touch customer keys or identifiable telemetry. Specifically they asked for:

- a current subprocessor roster (service, location, data types)
- the KMS/key custody lineage (who has the wrapping keys, HSM vendors, residency)
- a snapshot export of any custody/access logs you can share (time-bounded)

Can you confirm what you can provide by EOD PDT Wednesday? If anything requires a legal or compliance waiver, flag it and we'll loop legal.

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Solano
Security Manager, Novamed Health
Attachment: (none)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Solano <ava.solano@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Apr 2025 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: chainmap / custody ledger for SOC2 audit

Hi Ava — thanks for the heads up. We can deliver a concise package that covers the ask; plan below:

1) Subprocessor roster (CSV) with service name, country, data class touched, and contractual residency commitments.
2) KMS key lineage: an architecture diagram showing master key custody (cloud KMS / HSM partners), key wrapping flow, and who (role/team) has emergency access.
3) Custody/access snapshot: a redacted log export (start/end window you designate).

Notes:
- Full raw logs are sensitive; we can provide a time-bounded snapshot with user/role redaction.
- Anything that references customer ciphertext or PHI will be redacted per our privacy playbook; if Novamed's auditor needs unredacted records we will require a Data Processing Agreement addendum and a signed nondisclosure stipulation.

Deliverables and timing:
- redwood_subprocessor_chainmap_v1.csv (initial) — Wed 2025-04-30 11:00 PDT
- kms_keylineage_diagram.pdf — Wed 2025-04-30 14:00 PDT
- custody_ledger_snapshot_20250430.xlsx (redacted) — Wed 2025-04-30 16:00 PDT

I'll circulate the files to this thread and share a Drive link. Looping in Marissa for subprocessor inventory confirmation and Ben for the log extraction.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: (none)

From: Ava Solano <ava.solano@novamed.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novamed.com
Date: Tue, 29 Apr 2025 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: chainmap / custody ledger for SOC2 audit

Karthik — this looks great, appreciate the timeline. Two quick clarifications from our auditor:

- For the custody snapshot, they want an example of a key rotation event mapping (who performed rotation, key ids, timestamp, and resulting access change). If that triggers an exception, tell us and we will work through legal.
- For the subprocessor roster, please include the contract start date and whether each vendor has a SOC/ISO attestation on file (yes/no).

Also — can you add a single line in the package indicating if any on-prem or private deployments use customer-managed KMS (we have 2 customers doing private deployments and auditors treat that differently).

If you prefer, we can open a DocuSign request for the NDA addendum now; I can attach it to our auditor record.

Best,
Ava
Attachment: (none)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Solano <ava.solano@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Apr 2025 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: chainmap / custody ledger for SOC2 audit

Hi Ava — sending the package per the timeline. Files attached and uploaded to a shared folder (link below). Summary of what we included:

- redwood_subprocessor_chainmap_v1.csv — includes vendor, region, data classes, contract start date, and "has_attestation" column (SOC/ISO) set to yes/no.
- kms_keylineage_diagram.pdf — shows master key wrap via AWS KMS (us-east-1) with HSM vendor details and RBAC roles that have emergency unwrap privileges.
- custody_ledger_snapshot_20250430.xlsx — redacted access events for the requested window plus a sample rotation event mapping (rotation id ROT-20250412, rotated_by: infra-keyops, timestamp: 2025-04-12T03:14:22Z).

Additional notes:
- On-prem/private deployments: we have a short appendix row for each customer that indicates whether customer-managed KMS is in use and the expected audit pathway.
- Legal: we did not include raw ciphertext or unredacted PHI. If Novamed's auditor needs that, please return the signed NDA addendum link and we'll proceed.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b-Chainmap-Redwood
DocuSign NDA addendum (if needed): https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/req-7890
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/novamed

Thanks — let us know if you need a brief walkthrough.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Security Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_chainmap_v1.csv (text/csv); kms_keylineage_diagram.pdf (application/pdf); custody_ledger_snapshot_20250430.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
